name: buffa (protobuf with zero-copy view types)
baseline: prost 0.14 decoding into and encoding from owned generated structs
verdict_reason: Decoding into owned structs, buffa and prost trade wins by message shape (prost 16-20% ahead on two of five shapes; the independent benchmark puts them within 11%). The large gains, up to 2.8x, come only from buffa's borrowed view types, a different API that prost lacks.
tier_reason: Published benchmark code with pinned rustc 1.96.0, LTO and codegen-units=1 on a named bare-metal CPU, plus an independent run in rust_serialization_benchmark with rustc and CPU stated.
claimed_speedup: buffa README, binary decode MiB/s (buffa owned, buffa view, prost): ApiResponse 575, 872, 550; LogRecord 572, 1,336, 481; AnalyticsEvent 123, 225, 148; GoogleMessage1 601, 786, 698; MediaFrame 10,619, 41,441, 6,002, with prost (bytes) 18,432 (owned vs prost 1.05x, 1.19x, 0.83x, 0.86x, 1.77x; view vs prost 1.59x, 2.78x, 1.52x, 1.13x, and 2.25x vs prost with bytes) (derived from page data). rust_serialization_benchmark: log decode 3.0463 ms vs 3.3833 ms, buffa borrowed decode 1.7834 ms (1.11x; 1.90x vs prost decode) (derived from page data); mesh decode 14.146 vs 14.186 ms, mesh encode 8.9798 vs 8.0827 ms (prost 1.11x faster) (derived from page data); mk48 encode 3.7747 vs 5.4524 ms (buffa 1.44x faster) (derived from page data)
workload: buffa: five message shapes (ApiResponse, LogRecord, AnalyticsEvent, GoogleMessage1, MediaFrame), throughput of binary decode and encode on one pinned core, median of five passes. rust_serialization_benchmark: log (HTTP request logs with many strings), mesh (triangle array), minecraft_savedata and mk48 game updates; encode and decode time per data set.
hardware: buffa: bare-metal Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, turbo off, performance governor, one isolated core. rust_serialization_benchmark: AMD EPYC 7763 (4 vCPUs, Microsoft hypervisor).
toolchain: buffa: rust 1.96.0, lto=true, codegen-units=1, 64-byte block alignment (-Cllvm-args=-align-all-nofallthru-blocks=6), protoc 33.1. rust_serialization_benchmark: rustc 1.101.0-nightly (2026-10-04).
one_liner: Pure-Rust protobuf with editions support; about even with prost on owned types, 1.1-2.8x faster decode through zero-copy views.
how_it_is_fast: Each message gets an owned type and a MessageView<'a> type that reads fields straight from the wire buffer, so strings and bytes are not copied or allocated. A lazy mode defers parsing of nested fields until accessed. The owned path is a conventional generated decoder, which is why it lands close to prost.
use_it_when: You decode large volumes of messages and only read some fields, so borrowed views avoid most allocation.
You need protobuf editions support in pure Rust.
skip_it_when: You decode into owned structs and expect a big speedup; the owned path is within about 20% of prost either way.
You rely on tonic's prost integration and do not want to change code generation.
You need JSON encoding speed: prost was 6-33% faster on JSON encode in buffa's own table.
caveats: buffa's headline tables were measured at buffa v0.8.0; the independent rust_serialization_benchmark run uses 0.9.2.
buffa's methodology applies 64-byte block alignment to every Rust implementation, which it says measures the layout a profile-guided build would reach rather than a plain cargo build.
The large MediaFrame and AnalyticsEvent gains in lazy mode (up to +9538%) skip parsing work the other decoders do; they are not like-for-like.
tradeoffs: View types carry a lifetime tied to the input buffer (OwnedView wraps the buffer for async use).
Young project (0.x) with a smaller user base than prost.
